More likely to cause a brain hemorrhage or cerebral edema. I am a respiratory therapist, we do something called postural drainage and chest physiotherapy (CPT) on patients with cystic fibrosis. Each session lasts 20 minutes or so and we do it 3-4 times a day. Yes, secretions are gravity dependent and placing someone in a reverse Trendelenburg position will help mobilize secretions. The fluid they are talking about is pulmonary edema. You have a membrane in your lung where gas exchange takes place, its called the alveolar capillary membrane (AC). If you have congestive heart failure (CHF) fluid is pushed through this membrane and it builds up in your lungs. You can cough it out, its more like a foam and it just keeps coming until you give the patient diuretics or medications to improve heart function. In the case with covid-19 I would think its not a pressure difference causing the pulmonary edema but more of a toxic insult that causes the AC membrane to become leaky or more permeable. We see the same thing with people who hang themselves. Once the person goes unconscious the body will attempt to breath but because the airway is closed off the negative pressure generated in the lung will pull fluid across the AC membrane and cause a negative pressure pulmonary edema. So to answer your question, yes we do sometimes place people in a upside down position to mobilize secretions with pneumonia but this will not work with pulmonary edema. The short term fix for pulmonary edema is to put in a endotube, put them on a ventilator and crank up the pressure (positive end expiratory pressure[PEEP]) to push the fluid back across the AC membrane.
